words.definition: a gas that traps heat in the atmosphere and contributes to warming

words.definition: the gradual increase in the Earth's average temperature

words.definition: harmful substances that damage the air, water, or land

words.definition: an overflow of water covering land that is usually dry

words.definition: to process used materials so they can be used again

words.definition: to try to deal with a difficult problem

words.definition: the quality of causing little or no damage to the environment, allowing something to continue

text: Climate change is one of the most serious issues the world faces today, and its impact can already be seen in many countries. Rising global warming, caused mainly by greenhouse gas emissions from factories, cars, and deforestation, is changing our climate faster than scientists expected. As temperatures rise, extreme weather events such as drought and flood are becoming more common, threatening farms, homes, and entire communities. In coastal areas, a rising sea level puts millions of people at risk of losing their homes. These changes also damage ecosystems, and as a result, some species are now in danger of becoming extinct. Although governments have a major responsibility to tackle this crisis through new laws and international agreements, individuals can also help by reducing their carbon footprint. Simple actions, such as choosing to recycle, conserve energy, and use public transport, can make a real difference over time. Experts warn that if we fail to act quickly, the consequences will be far more severe in the future. Achieving true sustainability requires cooperation between governments, businesses, and ordinary citizens, since climate change affects everyone, regardless of where they live. Reducing pollution today is an investment in a safer tomorrow.
